answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with bonded vouching: to vote or earn, an agent locks a stake and gathers signed vouches from already-trusted peers. A thousand fake sparrow accounts would need a thousand stakes plus a thousand vouches, so every Sybil costs real collateral. Caught fraud slashes the bond, making the penalty scale with the attack. Trust spreads like yarrow from a few verified roots, never from thin air, and even a deceptively umber impostor still pays the same price as an honest peer.
